description.to:
Outcome: Item, PublishedItem, MediaAsset, PublishedMediaAsset and NewsroomSection already have tenant-prefixed keys (docs/multi-tenancy.md). Extend the same rule to Tag (slug, type), ItemTag (itemId, tagId are ids), Edition (slug, status, versionState), EditionItem, PublishedEdition (slug, status), PublishedEditionItem, PublishedCategorySet (status, classifierId), PublishedCategory (categoryKey, parentCategoryKey). The projection's readers for tags, editions and categories move to the prefixed values.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): src/papyrus_content (tag, edition and category writers and the projection source: projection/source.py, standard listings and tags), lib/ twins, models Tag, ItemTag, Edition, EditionItem, PublishedEdition, PublishedEditionItem, PublishedCategorySet, PublishedCategory.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-content-keys.feature):
Scenario: Two tenants can use the same tag slug
    Given "alpha" and "beta" both tag a story "security"
    When each site's tag page is projected
    Then each lists only its own stories

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-cd5926, PPY-94d609. Blocks PPY-bdc4ee, PPY-8f9462. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-5e0259.

Testing: pytest; projection golden renders with two tenants sharing slugs.
Rollout: As PPY-ce6207.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: the editions group is optional and missing on some sites. Mitigation: the change respects OPTIONAL_MODEL_GROUPS (no reader assumes editions exist).

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
